alternatives.name: ast-grep
alternatives.why_not_default: Adopted, and it shares the structural-code-lane decision with c3 (decisions.json lines 606-654). Its only retained execution is weaker for this requirement. evidence/receipts/portable-cli-artifacts.json is a native_cli_e2e fixture that says it is 'not an LLM invocation or general quality benchmark' (lines 4 and 15). The initial command returned exit_code 1 with matched false (lines 53-67). The corrected --stdin run found 8 function definitions with the pattern 'function $NAME($$$ARGS) { $$$BODY }' (lines 110-125). That shows definition matching only: no references and no native model host. It stays useful as index-free exact syntax search when the question is a structural pattern. It does not beat the winners on 'exact source and references'. The quota-blocked Codex CLI attempt did not exercise either tool, so it counts against neither c1 nor c3.

Its speed and completeness claims 'need a relevant language/workload comparison' (catalogs/us-equities/star-audit.json lines 9884-9904). It is untested, not failed. open_gaps: No representative benchmark across repositories or languages; no global best code retriever is established (packet limitations).
No measured head-to-head comparison between Serena, codebase-memory-mcp, jCodeMunch and ast-grep; each passed only its own recorded scope.

codebase-memory-mcp is proven on one existing selected index (not a fresh public-repo index) and one CJS function at depth 1. Static edges do not show runtime execution, and coverage for new target languages or changed sources is unverified (native-cli-gaps.json line 110; decisions.json lines 629 and 635).
The Codex CLI static-graph counterpart was never exercised because of the quota block; only Codex Desktop covers that host.
Serena coverage is established only for configured languages: Bash historically, plus eight Python/CJS checks. Other language servers are unverified.
jCodeMunch returned exact functions but no references in the retained evidence. Symbol updates, deletions and recovery are not_established (decisions.json lines 685 and 712-714).
ast-grep evidence covers definition matching on one fixture after a corrected command. Reference search and model-hosted use are unverified.
jCodeMunch's estimated tokens avoided are not exact provider savings.

overturn_protocol.metric: Per question: whether the exact original source span and the reference/callee set were correct, against the total cost of indexing, retrieval and index maintenance, with native provider usage kept separate from tool estimates

overturn_when: Build a sealed task set in the target languages, anchored on fixtures/after.py and the Serena find_symbol recipe in blueprints/token-native-focus/saturation-audit.json (lines 7609-7625). Include the retained collect span-plus-callees question (source_lines 91-127, 4 callees) as a reference-retrieval item. Change the verdict if, on that set, any of the following holds: ast-grep, CodeGraph or another challenger returns more correct original source and references than Serena, codebase-memory-mcp or jCodeMunch at an acceptable total indexing, retrieval and maintenance cost; a winner fails its item; or a focused read makes jCodeMunch redundant on every item. Two caveats: the Serena anchor is a documented recipe that this audit did not re-certify (current_host_recertified_by_this_audit false, line 7609), and fixtures/after.py is a single two-line function. The sealed multi-language set does not yet exist in the repository.
why_selected:
The requirement is exact source and references first, with an index only when it answers the actual question. Each winner does a separate job that the evidence covers.

Serena (c5) retrieves exact symbols and references in configured languages. catalogs/foundation/decisions.json#language-symbols (lines 565-603) records that native symbol operations passed, plus eight fresh Python/CJS checks after a language-coverage repair. docs/full-stack-convergence.md lines 25-30 records a read-only task, including Serena source/callers, that both native clients completed with no tool-result failures and with independent review of the original streams. These are retained summaries; I did not open the underlying receipts.

codebase-memory-mcp (c3) is the static-graph lane for source spans plus references. This is corrected from round 1, based on receipts I opened. evidence/receipts/native-cli-gaps.json (kind native_model_e2e, lines 4 and 77-110) records a native Claude run in which search_graph and trace_path both passed (native_tool_results_is_error [false,false]). It returned the function collect in tools/ecosystem/linux-usage-report.cjs, source_lines [91,127], with direct_callees installation, sourcesFor, runParser and overlaps (callees_total 4). evidence/receipts/desktop-cli-workflows.json lines 4 and 25-40 records the same span and callees on Codex Desktop (search_exit 0, trace_exit 0). The Codex CLI attempt in native-cli-gaps.json lines 32-39 was blocked_before_tools (usage_limit_exceeded, tools_executed 0, static_graph not_exercised). That is an account limit before any tool ran, not a tool failure. Among the adopted candidates, this is the only reference retrieval I observed in a receipt.

jCodeMunch (c2) is the conditional scoped symbol index. decisions.json#scoped-symbol-index (lines 656-719) records exact function retrieval and bounded native client calls, with install, restart and cleanup accepted and recovery not_established. docs/token-native-saturation.md lines 3-10 and 18 record three things: a clean-prefix install, real MCP use and restart with the exact selected function retained; native uninstall; and both native clients passing a Context Mode/jCodeMunch task with six successful MCP calls. The retained limit matches the requirement's index clause: its search/source sequence was larger than a known focused read. It therefore wins only when it replaces broad reads.

No measured cross-tool comparison ranks these tools against each other. Each passed only its own recorded scope. The class is native_proven for c3 on the receipts I read, and native_proven by retained record for c5 and c2.
